# Per-worker tokens

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P1 · Who did it](../README.md#phase-1--who-did-it) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:worker-credentials` · **Epic:** [#50](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/50) · **Tickets:** 11 (8S 3M)

The control plane issues a separate token for each worker. The token is shown once, stored only as a hash, bound to exactly one proxy id (P1 has no prefix binding: each replica gets its own token, and autoscaled per-pod identity comes with P2 mTLS enrollment in p2-worker-ca), revocable and tracked by last use. Workers use it for /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest, and the token's bound proxy id becomes the identity the CP trusts instead of the self-reported header. The shared WARDEN_CP_TOKEN is retired through an explicit auth mode and a documented migration; dashboard writes use the CP's own admin token (`--admin-token-env`), so retiring the shared token never disables them. Workers need no code change: both `controlPlane.tokenEnv` and `central.tokenEnv` carry the worker's own token.

## How we build it

- Token format: `wwt_` + lowercase unpadded RFC 4648 base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes (52 characters after the prefix). Token id: `wt_` + 16 hex characters. The CP stores only sha256(token), which is enough for 256-bit random secrets. New cpstate migration `worker_tokens(id, name UNIQUE, proxy_id NOT NULL, token_hash UNIQUE, created_by, created_at, expires_at NULL, last_used_at NULL, revoked_at NULL, revoked_by NULL)`. Each token is bound to one exact proxy_id; there is no prefix binding in P1. At most 2 active tokens per proxy_id, so rotation can overlap. Plaintext is returned only by Create and never logged, audited, stored or returned by any GET.
- Requires cpstate, which exists only with --state-dir (W-P1-SSO-01). One resolver picks the worker auth mode at startup and logs it once: `open` (no legacy token, not strict: today's behaviour, anonymous callers accepted as kind=none, warning logged), `mixed` (legacy token configured: worker tokens or the legacy token, anonymous rejected), `strict` (`--require-worker-tokens`: worker tokens only). Strict without --state-dir, or strict together with a legacy token, fails startup. Strict without TLS fails startup unless `--allow-insecure-worker-auth` is set; any token mode without TLS logs a warning.
- Seam: `WorkerAuthenticator.Authenticate(r) (WorkerPrincipal{TokenID, TokenName, ProxyID, Kind token|legacy|none}, error)`, applied only to /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest. It replaces `policyServer.token`, the bearerOK call in `handleHeartbeat`, and the string token in `analytics.NewIngestHandler` (which takes an authorizer func, W-P1-WTOK-08; `analytics.StaticTokenAuthorizer` keeps the old behaviour for the worker's own aggregator at internal/worker/worker.go:646). `bearerOK` stays on /central/secrets under W-P1-SSO-06 rules, now with the CP admin token (W-P1-WTOK-07). A `wwt_` bearer is never accepted on /central/secrets, /dashboard/* or /auth/*, and never satisfies the dashboard write guard. A `wwt_` bearer goes only through the token path and never falls back to the legacy compare.
- Identity: for kind=token the principal's ProxyID is authoritative. Missing X-Warden-Proxy-ID resolves to the bound proxy_id. Only a header equal to the bound id is accepted (exact match); any other value gets 403. The registry (SeenPolicyPull, SeenHeartbeat, SeenIngest), the stored AggregatedEvent.ProxyID and the ingest/events/MCP/secrets callbacks use the principal's id, never the raw header. Legacy and none principals keep using the header and are shown as unverified.
- Hot path: an in-memory index from hash to token is the only per-request lookup (one sha256 and one map read, no DB I/O). It is rebuilt after in-process Create/Revoke and reloaded when a 2s poll of SQLite `PRAGMA data_version` changes, which picks up writes from the bootstrap CLI process. A reload error keeps the last good index and never fails open. expires_at is checked against the CP clock only. `last_used_at` is updated in memory and flushed in one transaction every 60s and on shutdown.
- Revocation (held long-polls: W-P1-WTOK-09) is a soft delete (revoked_at set, row kept). Every /policy response (200 or 304) is re-authenticated before it is written, and an in-process revoke cancels that token's held long-polls through a per-token cancel registry so they return 401 at once. Bounds: API revoke takes effect on the next request; CLI revoke within 2s. Missing, malformed, unknown, expired and revoked tokens all get the same 401 body `unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; a binding failure gets 403 `proxy id mismatch`. The reason goes only to a rate-limited `worker auth rejected` log line, never the token or its hash.
- Admin surfaces: `GET/POST /dashboard/api/worker-tokens` and `DELETE /dashboard/api/worker-tokens/{id}`, admin role through the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table. With console.auth=none, POST and DELETE return 403 pointing to the CLI. The offline CLI `warden control-plane token create|list|revoke --state-dir` works with or without a running CP. `create --from-env VAR|--from-file F` registers an operator-generated `wwt_` value (format checked, only the hash stored), so compose and Kubernetes Secrets can supply the value; re-running it with the same name and value is a no-op.
- Audit: only token create and revoke are admin-audit events (target `worker_tokens`, auth_method oidc|breakglass|cli). Worker-plane routes (/policy, /control/heartbeat, /central/ingest) are excluded from the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware. CLI appends must keep the chain linear across processes (append inside a SQLite `BEGIN IMMEDIATE` transaction that reads prev_hash inside it).
- Observability: dashboard.WorkerView gains `tokenName`, `tokenLastUsed`, `authKind` (token|legacy|none) and `legacyRequests`; the fleet view shows a legacy/unverified badge. The CP has no /metrics endpoint in P1, so an in-memory counter `warden_cp_worker_auth_total{kind,outcome}` (bounded labels, no proxy_id) is kept and exported when the CP metrics endpoint lands (W-P5-RETN-06). Legacy request tracking per proxy id is capped at 10,000 ids.
- Migration: `--legacy-token-env` (with `--token-env` kept as a deprecated alias) keeps the shared token working for workers, so an upgraded CP behaves as before until tokens are issued. The CP's dashboard writes and /central/secrets authenticate with its own admin token, `--admin-token-env` (W-P1-WTOK-07), which falls back to the shared token only while no admin token is set, so strict mode never disables them. In strict mode with console.auth=none and no admin token, dashboard writes are refused by the fail-closed write guard and /central/secrets is not mounted, because its only gate would otherwise be empty. A revoked worker keeps enforcing its last-known-good, default-deny policy, gets no updates and cannot heartbeat or ingest; stopping its traffic means stopping the worker. Hand-off to P2: W-P2-WCA-04 extends WorkerAuthenticator with mTLS principals, and /central/secrets stays a human route in both phases.

## Done when

On a CP running with --state-dir and TLS, two workers use distinct per-worker tokens, one created in the console and one with the bootstrap CLI against the running CP. Each worker's /policy, heartbeat and ingest succeed with no worker code change, and events and fleet rows are attributed to each token's bound proxy id; a request with a spoofed X-Warden-Proxy-ID gets 403. A worker token is rejected on /central/secrets. Revoking one token in the console makes its next request on all three endpoints return 401 and a held long-poll return 401 at once; a CLI revoke takes effect within 2s. The other worker keeps working, and the revoked worker keeps its last-known-good default-deny policy. Tokens and revocations survive a CP restart. Create and revoke appear in the admin audit log with the correct actor, and worker-plane traffic does not. The plaintext appears only in the create response or CLI output. A CP started with --require-worker-tokens logs auth_mode=strict, rejects WARDEN_CP_TOKEN with 401 and refuses to start without --state-dir; dashboard writes and /central/secrets keep working with the CP admin token (`--admin-token-env`) and are never accepted with a worker token. The control-plane compose recipe and the e2e stack come up with per-worker tokens, a CP admin token and no WARDEN_CP_TOKEN; the other recipes follow, and a compromised-token runbook exists.

### 1/11 · W-P1-WTOK-01

**Add worker token store with hashed storage, revocation and in-memory index**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#51](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/51)

**Context.** Today every worker and the control plane (CP) share one bearer token, so a leaked token cannot be revoked per worker and the CP trusts a self-reported proxy id. Per-worker tokens give each worker its own revocable credential bound to one proxy id. This ticket is the foundation: the `worker_tokens` cpstate migration and a `WorkerTokenStore` that creates, authenticates, revokes and lists tokens. Only sha256 of the token is stored and the plaintext is returned once by `Create`. Authentication reads an in-memory index so the request path does no DB I/O, and the index reloads when another process (the offline CLI, W-P1-WTOK-05) writes the same SQLite file. Nothing calls the store yet, so this merges with no behaviour change. (The GitHub issue #51 carries both `size:S` and `size:M` labels; it is M.) Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** authenticating requests with it (W-P1-WTOK-02), cancelling held long-polls on revoke (W-P1-WTOK-09; this ticket only provides the `OnRevoked` hook it needs), the admin API (W-P1-WTOK-03) and the CLI (W-P1-WTOK-05).

**What to build.** Migration, store with token format, limits, index, `data_version` reload loop and last-used flushing. Requires cpstate, which exists only with `--state-dir` (W-P1-SSO-01); without it no store exists.

**Requirements**

- Migration `workertokens/0001` registered through the internal/cpstate runner (W-P1-SSO-01), passed to the cpstate open call in `controlplane.Run` when a state dir is set: `worker_tokens(id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, name TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL, proxy_id TEXT NOT NULL, token_hash BLOB UNIQUE NOT NULL, created_by TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NULL, last_used_at INTEGER NULL, revoked_at INTEGER NULL, revoked_by TEXT NULL)` with an index on proxy_id (no prefix column: each token is bound to one exact proxy_id; P1 has no prefix binding, and autoscaled per-pod identity comes with P2 enrollment in p2-worker-ca). Exported `controlplane.WorkerTokenMigrations()` for callers that open the DB themselves (the CLI).
- Token = `wwt_` + lowercase unpadded RFC 4648 base32 of 32 crypto/rand bytes (52 characters after the prefix); id = `wt_` + 16 hex; name 1-64 characters; proxy_id matches `^[A-Za-z0-9._-]{1,128}$`. Malformed input is rejected before hashing or any lookup. Only sha256(token) is stored (enough for 256-bit random secrets).
- API in internal/controlplane/workertokens.go (new): `NewWorkerTokenStore(db *cpstate.DB, opts StoreOptions{Clock, FlushInterval, PollInterval}) (*WorkerTokenStore, error)`; `Create(ctx, CreateOpts{Name, ProxyID, ExpiresAt, Actor, Plaintext}) (plaintext string, Token, error)` (an empty Plaintext generates one; a supplied one is format-checked and registered as an import); `Authenticate(plaintext) (Token, error)` returning `ErrMalformed`, `ErrUnknown`, `ErrRevoked` or `ErrExpired`; `Revoke(ctx, id, actor)` idempotent, `ErrNotFound` for an unknown id; `List(ctx)` metadata only; `MarkUsed(id, t)`; `OnRevoked(func(id string))` (called on in-process Revoke and when a reload finds newly revoked ids; used by W-P1-WTOK-09).
- At most 2 active (not revoked, not expired) tokens per proxy_id, so rotation can overlap; a third Create returns `ErrTooManyActive`. Create with an existing name returns `ErrNameTaken`, unless it is an import whose name and hash match an active row, which is a no-op.
- Revocation is a soft delete (revoked_at and revoked_by set, row kept). `Authenticate` reads only an in-memory hash-to-token index (one sha256 and one map read, no DB I/O). The index is rebuilt after in-process Create/Revoke and reloaded when `PRAGMA data_version` changes, polled every 2 s by `Run(ctx)` (the data_version approach is local to this store; it is not shared with other stores, to keep tickets independent). A reload error keeps the last good index, logs a warning and never fails open. `expires_at` is checked against the CP clock only (the clock port).
- `MarkUsed` updates memory only; dirty `last_used_at` values are flushed in one transaction every 60 s (interval injectable for tests) and by `Flush(ctx)` on shutdown.
- Plaintext is returned only by `Create` and never logged, audited, stored or returned by any later call. `Token.String()` and slog `LogValue` print only id, name and binding. No log, error message or test output contains the plaintext or the hash.
- Group the exported error values and keep the store free of HTTP concerns so a later Postgres backend can replace the data_version polling behind the same methods.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/controlplane/workertokens_test.go (store, DB-file scan, two stores on one file, fake clock, flush batching) and the allocation test.
2. internal/controlplane/workertokens.go (new): types Token, CreateOpts, error values, migration, NewWorkerTokenStore that loads the index.
3. Implement Create (generate or import, validate, enforce the active-per-proxy_id limit, insert, update index), Revoke, List and Authenticate (prefix and length check, sha256, map read, revoked/expired checks).
4. Implement `Run(ctx)`: ticker that reads PRAGMA data_version every 2 s and reloads the index on change (firing OnRevoked for newly revoked ids), flushes MarkUsed state every 60 s; implement Flush(ctx).
5. internal/controlplane/run.go: pass WorkerTokenMigrations to the cpstate open call when a state dir is set (construction of the store and use are W-P1-WTOK-02).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given a created token, the DB file does not contain the plaintext (bytes.Contains on the file) and token_hash equals sha256(plaintext): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStoreHashedAtRest`.
- [ ] Authenticate returns ErrRevoked for a revoked token, ErrExpired after expires_at (fake clock), ErrUnknown for a well-formed unknown token, and ErrMalformed for a value without the `wwt_` prefix or with the wrong length: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStoreAuthenticate`.
- [ ] A token created and then revoked through a second WorkerTokenStore on the same DB file (the CLI case) authenticates and then fails with ErrRevoked in the first store within one 2s poll interval, and OnRevoked fires for it: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStoreCrossProcessReload`.
- [ ] A reload error keeps the last good index (revoked tokens stay revoked, valid ones keep working) and logs a warning: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStoreReloadErrorKeepsIndex`.
- [ ] 10,000 MarkUsed calls for 3 tokens in one interval produce exactly one write transaction, and Flush writes pending values: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStoreMarkUsedBatching`.
- [ ] A third active token for the same proxy_id returns ErrTooManyActive; re-importing the same name and value is a no-op; an import with a malformed value is rejected before any DB access: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWorkerTokenStoreLimits|TestWorkerTokenStoreImport'`.
- [ ] No log line or error contains the plaintext or the hash (log capture): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStoreNoSecretsInLogs`.
- [ ] A cache-hit lookup allocates at most 2 times and 1000 lookups finish in under 50 ms in total (`go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenAuthenticateAllocs`, using `testing.AllocsPerRun` and a generous wall-clock bound); `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokenStore` and `scripts/check.sh` pass.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-SSO-01`](console-sso-rbac.md#111--w-p1-sso-01) Add internal/cpstate SQLite state store with migrations

**Unblocks:** [`W-P1-WTOK-02`](worker-credentials.md#211--w-p1-wtok-02) Authenticate /policy, heartbeat and ingest with per-worker tokens; [`W-P1-WTOK-05`](worker-credentials.md#511--w-p1-wtok-05) Add offline worker token bootstrap CLI; [`W-P1-OPS1-04`](ops-hardening.md#711--w-p1-ops1-04) Add the verified restore command

### 2/11 · W-P1-WTOK-02

**Authenticate /policy, heartbeat and ingest with per-worker tokens**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#52](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/52)

**Context.** With a token store (W-P1-WTOK-01) and a pluggable ingest authorizer (W-P1-WTOK-08), this ticket adds `WorkerAuthenticator` in internal/controlplane and applies it once to the three worker routes `/policy`, `/control/heartbeat` and `/central/ingest`, replacing the three separate shared-token checks. The token's bound proxy id becomes the identity the registry and ingest store record instead of the self-reported header. The default stays as today: with no worker tokens issued, a CP with a shared token behaves exactly as before, and a CP with no token stays open with a warning. `/central/secrets` keeps its own gate and never accepts a worker token. It was split from the original W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52): the ingest refactor is W-P1-WTOK-08 and held long-poll re-authentication is W-P1-WTOK-09. Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** strict mode, the new flags and the migration docs (W-P1-WTOK-04), cancelling held long-polls (W-P1-WTOK-09), the admin API (W-P1-WTOK-03), the CLI (W-P1-WTOK-05) and the CP's own dashboard-write token (W-P1-WTOK-07).

**What to build.** The authenticator with principal types and mode resolver, proxy-id binding, registry updates, the rejection logger and counters, and the `wwt_` rejection on human routes.

**Requirements**

- internal/controlplane/workerauth.go (new): `WorkerAuthenticator.Authenticate(r *http.Request) (WorkerPrincipal, error)` with `WorkerPrincipal{TokenID, TokenName, ProxyID string; Kind token|legacy|none}`. A `wwt_` bearer goes only to `WorkerTokenStore.Authenticate` and never falls back to the legacy compare; any other bearer is compared in constant time with the shared (legacy) token `Config.Token`. Errors: `ErrUnauthorized` (401) and `ErrProxyIDMismatch` (403).
- Mode is resolved once at startup and logged as `auth_mode=...`: `open` (no legacy token configured: today's behaviour, anonymous callers are accepted as kind=none and a warning is logged), `mixed` (legacy token configured: worker tokens or the legacy token, anonymous rejected). `strict` (worker tokens only) is added by W-P1-WTOK-04; the resolver is written so adding it is one case. Any token mode without TLS logs a warning.
- Applied only to `/policy`, `/control/heartbeat` and `/central/ingest` (ingest through the W-P1-WTOK-08 authorizer adapter, so the stored `AggregatedEvent.ProxyID` and every ingest callback use `principal.ProxyID`). `bearerOK` remains only on `/central/secrets`, `/central/secrets/{key}` and the dashboard, and a `wwt_` bearer there gets 401 for every method. A `wwt_` bearer never satisfies the dashboard write guard (`dashboardWriteGuard`, internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go) and never opens `/dashboard/*` or `/auth/*`.
- Binding (kind=token): the principal's ProxyID is authoritative. A missing `X-Warden-Proxy-ID` resolves to the bound proxy_id; a header equal to the bound id (exact match only, no prefix matching) is accepted; any other value gets 403 `proxy id mismatch`. Legacy and none principals keep using the header and are shown as unverified. The registry (`SeenPolicyPull`, `SeenHeartbeat`, `SeenIngest`) and the ingest/events/MCP/secrets callbacks always use the principal's id, never the raw header.
- Missing, malformed, unknown, expired and revoked tokens all get the same 401 body `unauthorized` with `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer`; the reason goes only to a `worker auth rejected` log line (reason, token_id when known, remote_addr), rate-limited to once per reason and remote_addr per minute (bounded map); the Authorization header, plaintext and hash are never logged.
- Successful requests call `MarkUsed` (memory only) and record Kind, TokenID and TokenName on the registry entry (internal/controlplane/registry.go); legacy requests increment a per-proxy-id counter capped at 10,000 ids (`legacyRequests`). In-memory counters `warden_cp_worker_auth_total{kind,outcome}` (bounded labels, no proxy_id) are kept for later export; the CP has no /metrics endpoint in P1 (W-P5-RETN-06).
- Wiring in `controlplane.Run` / `New`: when cpstate is open, construct the `WorkerTokenStore`, start `Run(ctx)`, `Flush` on shutdown, new `Config.WorkerTokens *WorkerTokenStore` (nil without state), build the authenticator and use it in `ServePolicy` (replacing `policyServer.token`), `handleHeartbeat` (replacing `bearerOK`) and ingest. Hand-off to P2: W-P2-WCA-04 extends the authenticator with mTLS principals.
- Worker-plane routes are excluded from the W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware (a classification, not code here).

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane/workerauth_test.go: a table over the three routes for valid, mismatched, missing-header, revoked and legacy cases.
2. New internal/controlplane/workerauth.go: WorkerPrincipal, WorkerAuthenticator, the mode resolver, binding check, rate-limited rejection logger, counters.
3. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go: replace the `token` field and inline compare in ServePolicy with the authenticator; call registry.SeenPolicyPull(principal.ProxyID). internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add Config.WorkerTokens, build the authenticator in New(), use it in handleHeartbeat, wire ingest with the adapter; leave bearerOK on handleSecrets/handleSecretByKey and reject `wwt_` bearers there and in the dashboard write guard.
4. internal/controlplane/registry.go: record Kind, TokenID and the legacy request count on SeenPolicyPull, SeenHeartbeat and SeenIngest.
5. internal/controlplane/run.go: construct the store and run its loops when cpstate is open; log the resolved mode.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Token A bound to `worker-1` with header `worker-2` gets 403 on all three endpoints; without the header all three succeed and the registry lists `worker-1`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerAuthBinding`.
- [ ] A token bound to `worker-1` gets 403 `proxy id mismatch` with X-Warden-Proxy-ID `worker-10` or `worker-1-a` (no prefix matching): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerAuthExactBinding`.
- [ ] After A is revoked, its next request on each endpoint returns 401 with body `unauthorized` while token B for `worker-2` keeps getting 200/204: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerAuthRevoked`.
- [ ] A valid `wwt_` token gets 401 on POST, GET and DELETE /central/secrets and cannot satisfy a dashboard write (no state change): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWorkerAuthRejectedOnHumanRoutes|TestWorkerTokenNeverSatisfiesWriteGuard'`.
- [ ] An ingest batch sent with token A and no header is stored with AggregatedEvent.ProxyID `worker-1` and the ingest callbacks receive `worker-1`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerAuthIngestProxyID`.
- [ ] Mixed mode rejects anonymous callers and accepts the legacy token (kind legacy, legacy count incremented); open mode accepts anonymous callers and logs the warning once: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerAuthModes`.
- [ ] Rejections log once per reason and remote_addr per minute and never contain the header, plaintext or hash (log capture): `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerAuthRejectionLog`.
- [ ] Existing shared-token tests pass unchanged: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWorkerAuth|TestPolicyTokenAuth|TestHeartbeatEndpoint|TestLongPollETag'` and `go test ./internal/analytics -run 'TestCentralIngest|TestIngest'`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 3/11 · W-P1-WTOK-03

**Add worker token admin API and fleet auth fields**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#53](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/53)

**Context.** Admins need to create, list and revoke worker tokens from the console API and see in the fleet view how each worker authenticates. This ticket adds the admin API (plaintext returned once, `Cache-Control: no-store`), the dashboard seam, role entries, audit rows and the new `WorkerView` fields. Mutations need the admin role; create and revoke are recorded by the admin audit middleware (W-P1-AAUD-02), which must not record worker-plane traffic. When admin audit is not enabled (`console.adminAudit.enabled` false) these rows simply do not exist. The panel is W-P1-WTOK-10 and the offline bootstrap CLI is W-P1-WTOK-05; this ticket was narrowed from the original W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) by moving the UI out. Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** the UI (W-P1-WTOK-10), strict mode (W-P1-WTOK-04), and cancelling long-polls (W-P1-WTOK-09).

**What to build.** Three routes behind a setter, authz and audit entries, and the registry-backed fleet fields.

**Requirements**

- `GET /dashboard/api/worker-tokens` returns 200 `[{id,name,proxyID,createdBy,createdAt,expiresAt,lastUsedAt,revokedAt}]`, including revoked tokens, never the hash or plaintext. `POST /dashboard/api/worker-tokens` with `{name, proxyID, expiresIn?}` returns 201 `{id,name,...,token}` with `Cache-Control: no-store`; 400 for invalid input (including an empty proxyID or an unknown field such as proxyIDPrefix), 409 for a taken name or too many active tokens. `DELETE /dashboard/api/worker-tokens/{id}` soft-revokes and returns 204, or 404 for an unknown id. Bodies are capped (8 KiB) and unknown fields rejected.
- Routes are wired through a new `dashboard.Server.SetWorkerTokens(WorkerTokenAdmin)` setter (internal/dashboard/dashboard_workertokens.go; not mounted on workers, so 404 there; register in `dashboard.Server.Handler()` next to `/dashboard/api/workers`, rule X9 baseline) and have admin entries in the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table. With `console.auth: none`, POST and DELETE return 403 `{"error":"use_cli"}` with a message pointing to `warden control-plane token` (no identity to attribute a mint to; the console would otherwise be an open credential minter); GET is allowed.
- `dashboard.WorkerView` gains `tokenName`, `tokenLastUsed`, `authKind` (token|legacy|none) and `legacyRequests`, filled in the `SetWorkers` closure (internal/controlplane/controlplane.go:424) from the registry data recorded by W-P1-WTOK-02.
- Create and revoke are audited by the W-P1-AAUD-02 middleware (Action `worker_token.create` / `worker_token.revoke`, Target `worker_tokens`, Audited true; target_ref `token:<id>`); register a `worker_tokens` StateHasher that hashes metadata only (id, name, proxy_id, expiry, revoked flag; never plaintext or hash). A test confirms the middleware never wraps `/policy`, `/control/heartbeat` or `/central/ingest`.
- The plaintext appears only in the 201 response of Create (never in later GETs, audit rows, logs or the hasher input). A `wwt_` bearer never authenticates any of these routes.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/dashboard/dashboard_workertokens_test.go (fake admin) and internal/controlplane tests for audit and exclusion. HTTP tests for dashboard writes authenticate like production: in `console.auth: none` with the CP dashboard-write bearer (on main `Config.Token`; after W-P1-WTOK-07 `Config.AdminToken`, which falls back to `Config.Token`), and in oidc mode with a session fixture from the SSO tests; a write without credentials is refused by the guard and a test asserts it.
2. New internal/dashboard/dashboard_workertokens.go: WorkerTokenAdmin interface, Server.SetWorkerTokens, handleWorkerTokens (GET/POST) and handleWorkerTokenByID (DELETE); register in dashboard.go Handler() and Routes().
3. internal/dashboard/dashboard.go: extend WorkerView with the new fields.
4. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: pass the WorkerTokenStore adapter to SetWorkerTokens and fill the new WorkerView fields.
5. Add the three routes to the authz table (admin; create/revoke Audited with Action and Target); register the worker_tokens StateHasher.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] An admin POST returns 201 with a `wwt_` token and `Cache-Control: no-store`; later GET bodies, the admin_audit row and all log lines contain neither the token nor its sha256: `go test ./internal/dashboard ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWorkerTokensAPI|TestWorkerTokensNoPlaintextAnywhere'`.
- [ ] A viewer or editor POST returns 403; with console.auth=none POST and DELETE return 403 use_cli and GET returns 200; a request with no session and no bearer is refused; the route-coverage test passes with the new routes: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWorkerTokensRoles|TestAuthzRouteCoverage'`.
- [ ] DELETE of an id sets revokedAt in the next GET and the token's next /policy request returns 401; an unknown id returns 404: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerTokensRevokeEffect`.
- [ ] One admin audit row is written per create and per revoke (when audit is enabled) with the right actor and no plaintext, and a heartbeat or ingest POST writes no audit row: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestWorkerTokensAudit|TestAuditSkipsWorkerRoutes'`.
- [ ] WorkerView carries tokenName, tokenLastUsed, authKind and legacyRequests for a token worker and a legacy worker: `go test ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard -run TestWorkerViewAuthFields`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 4/11 · W-P1-WTOK-04

**Add strict worker auth mode and the WARDEN_CP_TOKEN migration guide**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#54](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/54)

**Context.** This ticket adds the flags that move a CP from the shared token to per-worker tokens: `--legacy-token-env`, the deprecated `--token-env` alias, `--require-worker-tokens` and `--allow-insecure-worker-auth`, and the migration runbook. Strict mode rejects the shared token and needs `--state-dir` and TLS. Legacy use is shown per worker in the fleet view and in a rate-limited warning, since the CP has no metrics endpoint in P1. Dashboard writes and secret writes are NOT affected by these flags: they authenticate with the CP's own admin token (`--admin-token-env`, W-P1-WTOK-07), so removing the shared token never disables them. Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** the authenticator (W-P1-WTOK-02), the admin token (W-P1-WTOK-07), recipe changes (W-P1-WTOK-06/11).

**What to build.** Flag handling and validation in `controlplane.Params`/`Run`, the strict case of the mode resolver, the legacy warning, and docs/control-plane.md.

**Requirements**

- `--legacy-token-env` added; `--token-env` kept as an alias marked deprecated with `cmd.Flags().MarkDeprecated`. Setting both to different env var names is a startup error. Default unset, so behaviour is unchanged. Flags are parsed in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go and carried in `controlplane.Params` (`LegacyTokenEnv`, `RequireWorkerTokens`, `AllowInsecureWorkerAuth`); validation lives in `controlplane.Run`, not cmd/proxy (rule C1). The legacy token feeds ONLY worker authentication (and, as the documented fallback of W-P1-WTOK-07, the dashboard write guard when `--admin-token-env` is unset).
- `--require-worker-tokens` (default false) needs `--state-dir` and must not be combined with a legacy token; it needs TLS (`--ca-cert`/`--ca-key`) unless `--allow-insecure-worker-auth` is set. Each violation exits non-zero before listening, with an error naming the flag. In strict mode the resolver (W-P1-WTOK-02) accepts worker tokens only: any non-`wwt_` bearer, including the old shared token, gets 401.
- Startup logs one line with `auth_mode=open|mixed|strict`, whether a legacy token is configured (never its value), TLS on/off and the active worker token count. Token auth without TLS logs a warning.
- Strict mode without a CP admin token: if neither `--admin-token-env` nor a legacy token is configured, dashboard writes are refused by the write guard (fail closed) and an ERROR line says `dashboard writes are disabled: set --admin-token-env`, and `/central/secrets` is not mounted (404) so the secret-write API never falls back to open. With `--admin-token-env` set, both keep working in strict mode (the common production setup).
- Legacy-authenticated requests log `legacy worker token in use` once per proxy id per hour, tracked in a bounded set of 10,000 ids with an injectable clock, and increment the registry `legacyRequests` shown by `WorkerView` (W-P1-WTOK-03).
- docs/control-plane.md: migration steps (upgrade with `--legacy-token-env` and set `--admin-token-env`; create one token per worker; point both `controlPlane.tokenEnv` and `central.tokenEnv` at it and set a stable `central.proxyID`; confirm no legacy badge; restart with `--require-worker-tokens`; unset the shared env), the rotation flow (overlapping tokens: at most 2 active per proxy id), one token per replica with its own stable `central.proxyID` (P1 has no prefix binding; autoscaled pools move to P2 enrollment, W-P2-WCA), and revoked-worker behaviour (it keeps its last-known-good default-deny policy and cannot heartbeat or ingest).

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: cmd/proxy/controlplane_test.go (TestControlPlaneAuthFlags) and internal/controlplane/workerauth_test.go (TestWorkerAuthModes strict cases).
2. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the flags, the deprecation alias and the Params fields. internal/controlplane/run.go: validation of the combinations and the startup log line.
3. internal/controlplane/workerauth.go: strict mode rejects non-`wwt_` bearers with 401; add the hourly legacy warning with a bounded map and an injectable clock.
4. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: skip mounting /central/secrets in the strict, no-admin-token case and log the error.
5. docs/control-plane.md: runbook, rotation and revocation sections.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With --require-worker-tokens and --state-dir, the shared token gets 401 on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest and the startup log contains `auth_mode=strict`: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerAuthModesStrict`.
- [ ] --require-worker-tokens without --state-dir, with --legacy-token-env, or without TLS and without --allow-insecure-worker-auth exits non-zero before listening, naming the flag; `--token-env` and `--legacy-token-env` set to different names is an error: `go test ./cmd/proxy ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestControlPlaneAuthFlags|TestRunStrictValidation'`.
- [ ] `--token-env WARDEN_CP_TOKEN` starts in mixed mode with a deprecation notice; legacy requests from one proxy id log once per hour (fake clock) and WorkerView shows authKind=legacy: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestLegacyWorkerTokenWarning`.
- [ ] In strict mode with console.auth=none, `--admin-token-env` set: dashboard writes and /central/secrets work with the admin token; without any admin or legacy token: dashboard writes return the guard's refusal, /central/secrets returns 404 and an error line names `--admin-token-env`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestStrictModeAdminTokenKeepsWrites|TestStrictModeNoAdminTokenFailsClosed'`.
- [ ] docs/control-plane.md contains the migration steps, the rotation flow and the flag names: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestWorkerAuthDocsMentionFlags`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-WTOK-02`](worker-credentials.md#211--w-p1-wtok-02) Authenticate /policy, heartbeat and ingest with per-worker tokens; [`W-P1-WTOK-03`](worker-credentials.md#311--w-p1-wtok-03) Add worker token admin API and fleet auth fields; [`W-P1-WTOK-07`](worker-credentials.md#711--w-p1-wtok-07) Add --admin-token-env to the control plane for the dashboard write guard

### 5/11 · W-P1-WTOK-05

**Add offline worker token bootstrap CLI**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#235](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/235)

**Context.** The first worker tokens must be creatable before any admin can log in and while a CP is running. This ticket adds `warden control-plane token create|list|revoke`, which opens cpstate in `--state-dir` directly. `create --from-env` and `--from-file` register an operator-generated value, which lets compose and Kubernetes Secrets supply tokens without a worker code change. Create and revoke are written to the admin audit log with auth_method `cli` through the shared opener `adminaudit.OpenForCLI` (W-P1-AAUD-05), which uses the existing audit key and never creates one. Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** the store (W-P1-WTOK-01), the console API (W-P1-WTOK-03) and compose use (W-P1-WTOK-06).

**What to build.** Three subcommands that stay thin (rule C1) over `WorkerTokenStore`.

**Requirements**

- `token create --name N --proxy-id P [--expires-in D] [--from-env VAR | --from-file F] [--out F] [--admin-audit-key-file F]`, `token list [--json]`, `token revoke --id ID`; each takes a required `--state-dir` and works with or without a running CP. `list` opens the DB read-only (`cpstate.OpenReadOnly`); create and revoke open it read-write with `controlplane.WorkerTokenMigrations()`.
- Without --from-env/--from-file, create prints the plaintext once to stdout, or writes it to --out with mode 0600 and prints only the id. With an imported value, the plaintext is never printed.
- Imported values must pass the `wwt_` format check. Re-running create with the same name and value is a no-op that exits 0; the same name with a different value exits non-zero. Exit codes: 1 validation, 2 unknown id on revoke.
- Create and revoke append an admin audit row (auth_method `cli`, actor `cli:<os user>`, action `worker_token.create`/`worker_token.revoke`, target `worker_tokens`, target_ref `token:<id>`, details holding id, name and binding only) through `adminaudit.OpenForCLI`: with admin_audit rows present and a missing or mismatching key the CLI exits non-zero and writes nothing; when the table does not exist the append is skipped with a one-line notice. Appends stay linear when the CP and the CLI write at the same time (W-P1-AAUD-01 `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`).
- A running CP sees a CLI create or revoke within 2 s (W-P1-WTOK-01 `data_version` reload). No log line or error contains the plaintext or hash. cmd/proxy holds only flag parsing; the logic is in internal/controlplane.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in cmd/proxy/controlplane_token_test.go (state dir shared with an httptest CP).
2. New cmd/proxy/controlplane_token.go: newControlPlaneTokenCmd() with create, list and revoke, added under newControlPlaneCmd() in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.
3. Each subcommand opens `<state-dir>/warden-cp.db` through cpstate and calls WorkerTokenStore (W-P1-WTOK-01), then closes it; audit through adminaudit.OpenForCLI.
4. Document the commands in docs/control-plane.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With a CP running on --state-dir D, `warden control-plane token create --name w2 --proxy-id worker-2 --state-dir D --out f` creates f with mode 0600, and a /policy request with its contents gets 200 within 2s and no restart: `go test -race ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneTokenCmd`.
- [ ] `WARDEN_WORKER_1_TOKEN=wwt_... warden control-plane token create --name w1 --proxy-id worker-1 --from-env WARDEN_WORKER_1_TOKEN --state-dir D` run twice creates one row and prints no plaintext; a malformed value and a same-name different-value run exit non-zero: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneTokenImport`.
- [ ] `token revoke --id` on a running CP makes that token's next request return 401 within 2s; an unknown id exits 2: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestControlPlaneTokenRevoke`.
- [ ] After interleaved CLI and API creates and revokes, adminaudit.Verify returns ok and each action appears once with auth_method cli; with admin_audit rows present and the key file missing the CLI exits non-zero and creates no token: `go test ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestControlPlaneTokenAudit|TestControlPlaneTokenKeyMissing'`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-WTOK-01`](worker-credentials.md#111--w-p1-wtok-01) Add worker token store with hashed storage, revocation and in-memory index; [`W-P1-AAUD-05`](admin-audit-log.md#58--w-p1-aaud-05) Gate admin audit behind config, check the key id at startup, add segment rotation and a shared CLI recorder opener

### 6/11 · W-P1-WTOK-06

**Move the control-plane compose recipe and e2e stack to per-worker tokens**

Type **chore** · Size **S** · Issue [#236](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/236)

**Context.** The control-plane compose recipe, and the e2e stack that overlays it (`make e2e` = `docker-compose.control-plane.yml` + `docker-compose.e2e.yml`), still hand every container the shared `WARDEN_CP_TOKEN`. This ticket switches that stack to per-worker tokens and gives the CP its own admin token: a one-shot `cp-bootstrap` service registers each worker's token with `token create --from-env` on the shared state volume before the CP and workers start, the CP runs with `--require-worker-tokens` and `--admin-token-env=WARDEN_CP_ADMIN_TOKEN`, and workers keep reading their token from env, so no worker code changes. It also folds in the review addendum on #236: a compromised-token runbook. Because `deploy/compose/docker-compose*.yml` is a critical path, this PR also needs the L2 `e2e` job. The other recipes are W-P1-WTOK-11. Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** the other recipes and sample worker configs (W-P1-WTOK-11) and any binary change.

**What to build.** Compose, e2e override, harness token helper, worker configs used by this stack, a `.env.example` and docs.

**Requirements**

- deploy/compose/docker-compose.control-plane.yml: add a one-shot `cp-bootstrap` service (same image, `control-plane token create --from-env WARDEN_WORKER_N_TOKEN --name wN --proxy-id worker-N --state-dir=/data`, running as the CP's user on the `cp-data` volume) for each worker; the CP and the workers use `depends_on: condition: service_completed_successfully` on it. The CP runs with `--require-worker-tokens --admin-token-env=WARDEN_CP_ADMIN_TOKEN` and no `--token-env`/`WARDEN_CP_TOKEN`; TLS stays on.
- Each worker container gets its own token from `WARDEN_WORKER_1_TOKEN` / `WARDEN_WORKER_2_TOKEN` (host `.env`) mapped to the in-container variable `WARDEN_WORKER_TOKEN`, used by both `controlPlane.tokenEnv` and `central.tokenEnv`, and a stable `central.proxyID` (`WARDEN_PROXY_ID`). The shared worker config files therefore use `tokenEnv: WARDEN_WORKER_TOKEN` (configs/config.worker.yaml, config.e2e-worker.yaml, config.e2e-worker-transparent.yaml), so two workers can share one config file and still hold different tokens.
- deploy/compose/docker-compose.e2e.yml: the `environment: !override` blocks of worker-1, worker-2 and worker-3 (WARDEN_CP_TOKEN at the lines that set it) switch to per-worker tokens, and `cp-bootstrap` registers all three; the harness bearer for CP dashboard writes (`Target.ControlPlaneToken()` in test/harness/compose/lifecycle.go, used by test/e2e/fleet_test.go) returns `WARDEN_CP_ADMIN_TOKEN` (default `dev-cp-admin-token`). The existing worker admin token (`WARDEN_ADMIN_TOKEN`) is unrelated and unchanged.
- New deploy/compose/.env.example documents `WARDEN_WORKER_1_TOKEN`, `WARDEN_WORKER_2_TOKEN`, `WARDEN_WORKER_3_TOKEN` and `WARDEN_CP_ADMIN_TOKEN` with obviously fake dev values (valid `wwt_` format for the worker tokens); real values are never committed. Compose defaults (`${VAR:-...}`) use the same dev values so `make e2e` needs no setup.
- A static, Docker-free test (precedent: test/harness/compose/publish_test.go) parses the recipe and e2e override and asserts: no `WARDEN_CP_TOKEN` and no `--token-env` in the control-plane stack, the CP command has `--require-worker-tokens` and `--admin-token-env`, every worker `depends_on` cp-bootstrap with `service_completed_successfully`, and each worker's token variable differs.
- docs/control-plane.md quickstart is updated to the new recipe, and gains the compromised-token runbook (review addendum on #236): revoke the token (console `DELETE /dashboard/api/worker-tokens/{id}` or `warden control-plane token revoke`), watch the worker fail `/policy` and `/control/heartbeat` with 401 (the worker keeps enforcing its last-known-good default-deny policy but gets no updates), re-bootstrap a replacement with `token create` (overlap allowed: at most 2 active per proxy id), and use `last_used_at` / `tokenLastUsed` in the fleet view to spot a suspected leak (use from an unexpected time or after the worker was stopped).

### 7/11 · W-P1-WTOK-07

**Add --admin-token-env to the control plane for the dashboard write guard**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#461](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/461)

**Context.** Every dashboard write on the CP (`dashboard.SetWriteGuard` with `NewBearerWriteGuard`, internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go, added by #422/#425) and `/central/secrets` today accept the same single `--token-env` token that workers use to authenticate. The CP has no separate admin token (only workers have `--admin-token-env`). Once workers get their own tokens (this feature) the shared token goes away, and with it every dashboard write would silently be refused. This ticket gives the CP its own admin bearer, separate from the worker/legacy token, so strict worker-token mode (W-P1-WTOK-04) and the compose move (W-P1-WTOK-06) never disable dashboard writes. The SSO tickets call it the 'CP admin bearer'. In oidc mode sessions replace it for the console (W-P1-SSO-05/06). Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** worker authentication (W-P1-WTOK-02), the SSO session path, and compose changes (W-P1-WTOK-06).

**What to build.** The flag, the Params/Config field, one `dashboardWriteToken()` source of truth used by the dashboard write guard and the `/central/secrets` gate, a back-compat fallback and docs.

**Requirements**

- cmd/proxy/controlplane.go (parse only, rule C1): new flag `--admin-token-env` (env var holding the CP admin bearer; default unset) -> new `controlplane.Params.AdminTokenEnv`; `controlplane.Run` (internal/controlplane/run.go) resolves it into new `controlplane.Config.AdminToken`. A flag that names an empty env var logs a WARN (`control-plane: admin-token-env set but empty; dashboard writes will be refused`) and leaves AdminToken empty. The token value is never logged.
- New method `(*Server).dashboardWriteToken() string` (internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go): AdminToken when set, otherwise the legacy/shared `Config.Token` as a back-compat fallback with a one-time startup WARN (`dashboard writes use the shared worker token; set --admin-token-env`). `dashboardWriteGuard()` builds `NewBearerWriteGuard` from it and its ConfigHint becomes `Start it with --admin-token-env <ENV> (e.g. WARDEN_CP_ADMIN_TOKEN)`. With neither token the guard still fails closed (403 `dashboard writes are disabled`).
- `/central/secrets` and `/central/secrets/{key}` (human routes, internal/controlplane/secrets.go) use a new `adminBearerOK(r)` built on `dashboardWriteToken()` instead of `bearerOK`: when AdminToken is set the shared worker token no longer opens secret reads or writes (401). `bearerOK` itself is NOT changed (it keeps gating `/policy` and `/control/heartbeat` until W-P1-WTOK-02). When only the shared token is set the behaviour is exactly as today (fallback), and when no token of either kind is set the routes keep today's development-open behaviour (W-P1-SSO-06 and W-P1-WTOK-04 add the fail-closed rules). In oidc mode W-P1-SSO-06 replaces both with an admin session.
- Worker routes are unaffected: `/policy`, `/control/heartbeat` and `/central/ingest` never accept the admin token (a worker with the admin token gets 401 when a worker/legacy token is configured), and the admin token never authenticates as a worker principal.
- If AdminToken equals the shared token a WARN says they should differ (the point of the flag is separation); startup does not fail.
- docs/control-plane.md: document the flag, the fallback and that write scripts (`curl -H "Authorization: Bearer ..."` examples) must use the admin token once it is set; update the examples that use `$WARDEN_CP_TOKEN` for secrets.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first: internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth_test.go, secrets_test.go additions, cmd/proxy flag test.
2. cmd/proxy/controlplane.go: add the flag and Params.AdminTokenEnv. internal/controlplane/run.go: resolve the env into Config.AdminToken with the warnings. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: add Config.AdminToken.
3. internal/controlplane/dashboard_auth.go: dashboardWriteToken() and the guard; internal/controlplane/secrets.go: add adminBearerOK and use it in handleSecrets/handleSecretByKey (leave bearerOK alone).
4. docs/control-plane.md: flag, fallback and examples.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With `--admin-token-env` set to token A and `--token-env` to W: a dashboard write with W gets 401, with A succeeds; `/central/secrets` POST with W gets 401, with A succeeds: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAdminTokenSeparatesWriteAuth`.
- [ ] With only the shared token configured, dashboard writes and secret writes with it still succeed and a startup WARN names `--admin-token-env`; with no token at all writes get 403 `dashboard writes are disabled` mentioning `--admin-token-env`: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestAdminTokenFallbackToSharedToken|TestDashboardWritesRefusedWithoutAnyToken'`.
- [ ] The admin token gets 401 on /policy, /control/heartbeat and /central/ingest when a shared token is configured, and the shared token gets 401 on dashboard writes when an admin token is set: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run TestAdminTokenNotAWorkerCredential`.
- [ ] An empty env var logs the WARN and refuses writes; the token value never appears in logs (log capture): `go test ./internal/controlplane ./cmd/proxy -run 'TestAdminTokenEnvEmpty|TestAdminTokenNeverLogged|TestControlPlaneAdminTokenFlag'`.
- [ ] Existing CP tests that send `Config.Token` for writes pass unchanged: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane ./internal/dashboard ./cmd/proxy`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 8/11 · W-P1-WTOK-08

**Let the ingest handler take a pluggable authorizer instead of a static token**

Type **chore** · Size **S** · Issue [#462](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/462)

**Context.** `/central/ingest` is served by `analytics.NewIngestHandler(store, token)`, which compares one shared bearer string and takes the proxy id from the self-reported `X-Warden-Proxy-ID` header. Per-worker tokens (W-P1-WTOK-02) need the handler to ask a pluggable authorizer who the caller is, and to use the authorizer's proxy id for every stored event and callback. This ticket is that behaviour-neutral refactor, split from the original W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) in the 2026-10-19 pass because it touches only internal/analytics and its two call sites and can merge first. Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** the real authenticator (W-P1-WTOK-02). No behaviour changes in this ticket.

**What to build.** An authorizer function type, `StaticTokenAuthorizer`, and the call-site updates.

**Requirements**

- internal/analytics/central_http.go (existing): `type IngestAuthorizer func(r *http.Request) (proxyID string, status int)` where status 0 means accepted, otherwise the HTTP status to answer (401 `unauthorized`, 403 for a binding failure with its own text); `NewIngestHandler(store FleetStore, auth IngestAuthorizer) *IngestHandler`. The returned proxyID is used for `AggregatedEvent.ProxyID` and for every callback (`onIngest`, `onEvents`, `onMCP`, `onSecrets`).
- `analytics.StaticTokenAuthorizer(token string) IngestAuthorizer` reproduces today's behaviour exactly: an empty token accepts every request; otherwise the `Authorization` header must equal `Bearer <token>` (constant-time compare); the accepted proxy id is the `X-Warden-Proxy-ID` header value.
- Update the two production call sites: internal/controlplane/controlplane.go:342 (`NewIngestHandler(s.central, s.cfg.Token)` -> `StaticTokenAuthorizer(s.cfg.Token)`) and the worker's own aggregator at internal/worker/worker.go:646 (`os.Getenv(pol.Central.TokenEnv)`), and the analytics tests (central_http_test.go).
- No change to request/response shapes, limits (`maxIngestBytes`), status codes or log output; existing ingest tests pass with only constructor updates.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/analytics/central_http_test.go (authorizer returning a different proxy id than the header; status 401/403 passthrough).
2. internal/analytics/central_http.go: add IngestAuthorizer, StaticTokenAuthorizer; change NewIngestHandler; use the returned proxy id.
3. Update internal/controlplane/controlplane.go and internal/worker/worker.go call sites and existing tests.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A custom authorizer that returns proxyID `bound-1` for a request whose header says `spoofed` stores every event with ProxyID `bound-1` and passes `bound-1` to onIngest, onEvents, onMCP and onSecrets: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestIngestHandlerAuthorizerProxyID`.
- [ ] An authorizer returning 401 or 403 stops the request before the body is read and the response carries that status: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestIngestHandlerAuthorizerRejects`.
- [ ] `StaticTokenAuthorizer` accepts everything for an empty token, accepts only the exact bearer otherwise, and uses the header proxy id: `go test ./internal/analytics -run TestStaticTokenAuthorizer`.
- [ ] Existing ingest tests pass unchanged apart from the constructor: `go test -race ./internal/analytics ./internal/controlplane ./internal/worker -run 'TestCentralIngest|TestIngest|TestCentral'`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

### 9/11 · W-P1-WTOK-09

**Re-authenticate held long-polls and cancel them when their token is revoked**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#463](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/463)

**Context.** `/policy` is a long-poll: a worker holds a request open for up to 30 s (`controlPlane.longPollWait`). If a token is revoked while its request is parked, the worker must not receive another policy response, and the revoked worker should find out at once instead of at the end of the wait. This ticket makes every `/policy` response re-authenticate and lets a revoke cancel that token's held long-polls. It was split from the original W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52). A revoked worker keeps enforcing its last-known-good, default-deny policy, gets no updates and cannot heartbeat or ingest; stopping its traffic means stopping the worker. Siblings in the Per-worker tokens feature (epic #50): W-P1-WTOK-01 (#51) token store, W-P1-WTOK-08 ingest authorizer refactor, W-P1-WTOK-02 (#52) WorkerAuthenticator on /policy, heartbeat and ingest, W-P1-WTOK-09 held long-poll re-authentication and cancel on revoke, W-P1-WTOK-03 (#53) admin API and fleet fields, W-P1-WTOK-10 console panel, W-P1-WTOK-07 the CP's own admin token for dashboard writes, W-P1-WTOK-04 (#54) strict mode and migration guide, W-P1-WTOK-05 (#235) offline bootstrap CLI, W-P1-WTOK-06 (#236) control-plane and e2e compose move, W-P1-WTOK-11 remaining compose recipes.

**Out of scope here:** the authenticator itself (W-P1-WTOK-02) and the admin revoke surfaces (W-P1-WTOK-03, W-P1-WTOK-05).

**What to build.** A per-token cancel registry, a re-authentication before every `/policy` write, and the `OnRevoked` wiring.

**Requirements**

- internal/controlplane/workerauth.go: per-principal cancel registry (`map[tokenID]` of channels, created lazily when a token-kind long-poll parks, removed when it returns). `WorkerTokenStore.OnRevoked` (W-P1-WTOK-01) closes the token's cancel channel, for an in-process revoke at once and for a revoke made by the CLI process within the 2 s `data_version` reload.
- `policyServer.ServePolicy` (internal/controlplane/policyserver.go) re-authenticates before writing ANY response after a wait (200 and 304) and returns 401 `unauthorized` if the token is no longer valid; its select also listens on the token's cancel channel so a revoked token's held request returns 401 within 1 s. Revoked or expired tokens never get a 304.
- Waking N waiters does no DB I/O: re-authentication reads the in-memory index only. Waiters of other tokens are unaffected by a revoke.
- Kind legacy and none principals are not cancelled (they have no per-credential identity); their behaviour is unchanged.
- The cancel registry is keyed by token id so W-P2-WCA-04 can key it by worker id as well for cert principals.

**Implementation plan**

1. Write the tests first in internal/controlplane/workerauth_longpoll_test.go (httptest CP, injected clock where possible).
2. internal/controlplane/workerauth.go: cancel registry, OnRevoked hook registration at construction.
3. internal/controlplane/policyserver.go: select on the cancel channel; re-authenticate before the 200 and 304 writes.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A held `GET /policy?wait=30s` for token A returns 401 within 1s of an in-process revoke of A: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestLongPollRevokeCancels`.
- [ ] A revoke made through a second store on the same DB file (the CLI case) cancels the held request within 3s: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestLongPollRevokeFromOtherProcess`.
- [ ] A revoked token whose wait times out gets 401, not 304; a token revoked between a change and its response gets 401, not the new policy: `go test ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestLongPollRevokedNever304|TestLongPollRevokedNeverGetsNewPolicy'`.
- [ ] 500 waiters for token B stay parked and are all woken by a policy change with zero DB queries (query counter) while A's waiters get 401: `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestLongPollWakeNoDBIO`; `scripts/check.sh` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P1-WTOK-02`](worker-credentials.md#211--w-p1-wtok-02) Authenticate /policy, heartbeat and ingest with per-worker tokens

**Unblocks:** [`W-P2-WCA-04`](worker-mtls.md#48--w-p2-wca-04) Accept worker certs in WorkerAuthenticator and add /control/renew
